name: Mitochondrial Bioenergetics, ETC Complexes and Proton Gradient Uncoupling

reference.source: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry / Medical Biochemistry 5th ed
clinicalPearls: Complexes I, III, and IV pump protons from matrix to intermembrane space, generating the proton-motive force
ATP synthase (Complex V) couples proton transit back into the matrix to rotational catalysis of ATP synthesis
Cyanide and carbon monoxide block Complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase), halting electron transport and oxygen consumption
Uncouplers (2,4-dinitrophenol, aspirin overdose) dissipate the proton gradient, collapsing ATP synthesis while maximizing heat
Brown adipose tissue expresses thermogenin (UCP1) for non-shivering thermogenesis in neonates
reference.pathophysiology: Coupled oxidative phosphorylation requires an intact, ion-impermeable inner mitochondrial membrane. Inhibitors of electron transfer complexes arrest the respiratory chain, stopping both ATP generation and oxygen utilization, precipitating cytotoxic hypoxia and severe lactic acidosis. Chemical uncouplers increase membrane proton conductance, disconnecting electron transport from phosphorylation, dissipating energy as uncontrolled heat.
additionalDifferentials: Cyanide toxicity (high venous SvO2 with severe lactic acidosis) vs carbon monoxide poisoning
Salicylate toxicity (mixed early respiratory alkalosis and late metabolic acidosis with hyperthermia)
Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS)
additionalInvestigations: Arterial blood gas and serum lactate (severe lactic acidosis with elevated central venous oxygen saturation)
Blood cyanide level and carboxyhemoglobin fraction
Muscle biopsy with Gomori trichrome stain (ragged-red fibers in mitochondrial myopathies)
